digest.component_or_area: prompt caching and cache-prefix boundary placement in plan-review passes
propositions: Cache writes are emitted on every plan-review gate call and never read across calls because the marked cache breakpoint sits after pass-specific stance suffixes rather than at the shared_plan_prefix boundary, causing three different cache keys and no reuse within a single run.

The cache prefix embeds the whole plan by design (shared_plan_prefix = stance + plan text) so content-addressed caching cannot reuse the same prefix across different tickets; cross-ticket prefix identity is unsatisfiable without evicting the plan and destroying within-run warm-then-fan-out reuse.

Single-step passes (finder, verifiers, coach) write cache at premium rates and never read it within or across runs due to the breakpoint placement, incurring ~9200 tokens of pure write-premium waste per leaf plan review with zero benefit.
The existing cache-ineffectiveness diagnostic (write==0 AND read==0) does not flag the write-every-call/never-read shape, making this inefficiency invisible to telemetry.

Moving the cache breakpoint to the end of the byte-stable shared_plan_prefix boundary allows the Pass-1 finder write to be read by Pass-2 verifiers within a single run and enables same-ticket re-reviews within the TTL to read cached content.
